subject: Dedicated pool: traffic scenarios, GPU preference & benchmarking asks
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Porter <aporter@stratusml.com>, Jordan Patel <j.patel@novohealth.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + dedicated sizing asks (traffic scenarios)

Thanks for the time today — good discussion on workloads and latency targets. Quick recap and the specific asks so we can size a Dedicated pool that meets both steady-state TPS and burst needs.

Summary of the call:
- Use case: customer-facing assistant + nightly batch embedding job.
- Peak burst: spikes to 600 TPS for 2–6 minute windows during marketing events.
- Steady state: 45–65 TPS with 99th pct latency target of 250ms.
- Prompt profile: ~30 tokens warm prompt, 120 tokens generated on average.

Sizing asks (what we need from you):
1) Confirm token mix: percent requests that are short (<=64 out) vs long (>256 out).
2) Typical concurrency per user session (how many parallel requests per user?).
3) Any regional failover requirements (do you need multi-region Dedicated or Private fallback?).

Early thoughts from our side:
- For your burst profile we recommend reserved capacity with a small burst pool (20–30% of base) rather than pure autoscale — this keeps predictable latency during short spikes.
- H100s give ~1.6–2x better throughput on long generations vs A100 for the Llama2-derived models you mentioned, but quantized L4-like GPUs could be cost-effective for short outputs.

Attached: capacity_workbook.xlsx (please fill the traffic columns), and a CSV with the crude latency profile we recorded from the demo.

Next step: if you can send the token distribution and concurrency by Wed (22nd), Ben and Marissa will draft a Dedicated pool proposal with HW mix and a baseline cost estimate.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
[attachment: capacity_workbook.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Alex Porter <aporter@stratusml.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Patel <j.patel@novohealth.io>
Date: Tue, 21 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + dedicated sizing asks (traffic scenarios)

Appreciate the clear summary, Karthik. A few clarifications from our engineering team:

- Token mix: roughly 78% short responses (<=64 tokens out), 18% medium (65-255), 4% long (>256). We rarely do >512.
- Concurrency: most sessions send a single request at a time; heavy users can have 2–3 parallel tool calls (so plan for 3 concurrent per heavy session).
- Burst windows: marketing events are predictable (we give you calendar dates). Bursts are typically 3–5 mins, occasional up to 12 mins.
- Regional: US primary, EU read-only replica for GDPR customers later this year. For the pilot, US-only Dedicated is fine but we'd like a documented fallback plan (hosted API or cross-region).

We'll fill the workbook today and upload to the Drive link you gave. One ask from our infra side: can you include memory/KV cache sizing recommendations for when we pin long conversational state? We use a mix of conversation history (avg 600 tokens kept per user) and short tool outputs.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Porter | Head of Platform | StratusML
[attachment: latency_profile.csv (csv)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Porter <aporter@stratusml.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Dec 2026 11:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + dedicated sizing asks (traffic scenarios)

Nice, Alex — that's helpful. A couple of notes while we review the workbook:

- GPU recommendation: given the 4% long-generation tail and your 120-token average, I'm leaning toward an H100 + mixed A100 pool: H100s for the few long jobs and A100/quantized nodes for the short/medium requests to optimize cost. We'll model split ratios (e.g., 70% A100/quantized, 30% H100) and show latency envelopes.
- KV cache: we'll include an appendix with cache sizing; for 600 tokens/state per active session, please also include expected active session count. That drives total KV RAM and how many cache-shared nodes you need.
- Burst model: recommend a reserved burst buffer sized for the 95th pct burst size (you said 600 TPS peak) — we'll show both a conservative and aggressive buffer in the workbook.

Ben — can you run a quick simulated TPS run on our bench with 30/70 short/long distribution and send the run IDs? That will help justify the H100 increment in the proposal.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole | Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-dedicated-options.pdf (pdf)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Alex Porter <aporter@stratusml.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Dec 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + dedicated sizing asks (traffic scenarios)

Quick update — ran the bench jobs today (run IDs: RB-9921 / RB-9922). Highlights:
- 30/70 short/long mix at 250ms target: A100 nodes hit steady-state comfortably at 60 TPS/node for your model family; H100 improves long-request throughput ~1.8x and cuts 99p by ~40ms.
- With the 600 TPS burst profile simulated, the hybrid pool (70% A100 + 30% H100) plus a 25% reserved burst buffer keeps 99p < 250ms in 9/10 runs. The outlier run (no KV cache warm) showed a spike to ~420ms.

Action items now:
1) Alex: upload the workbook with expected active session numbers for peak windows (you said calendar events; if you can give attendee counts that helps).
2) Marissa/Karthik: I'll produce a short proposal doc with two capacity options (conservative and cost-optimized) by Thurs (Dec 30).
3) Alex: please confirm whether Private VPC is in scope for the pilot or just Dedicated in our tenancy — that'll change network configuration and KMS choices.

I'll attach the bench results CSV to the proposal.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
